title: A two-term computation for a procyclic group
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime number, $s\geq0$ an integer, and $A$ a finite ring killed by $\ell^s$. Let $G$ be the additive group of $\mathbf Z_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], with its usual inverse-limit topology $\mathbf Z_\ell=\varprojlim_{r\geq1}\mathbf Z/\ell^r\mathbf Z$, and let $\tau=1$ be its additive topological generator. For a discrete continuous $A[G]$-module $M$ and its continuous cohomology as in [def-exc-continuous-cohomology], that cohomology is computed by
$$
[\,M\xrightarrow{\tau-1}M\,]
\quad\text{in degrees }0,1,
$$
where $(\tau-1)m=\tau\cdot m-m$.

proof.text: Fix $A$ and $G$. The inverse-limit description in the statement makes $G$ profinite, with the kernels $\ell^rG$ of reduction modulo $\ell^r$ a neighbourhood basis at zero. Work in the abelian category $\mathcal C$ of discrete continuous $A[G]$-modules from [lem-exc-discrete-modules-abelian]. Define the functor $K:\mathcal C\to\operatorname{CochainComplex}(A\text{-Mod},\mathbf N)$ by $K(M)^0=K(M)^1=M$, $d^0=\tau-1$, and zero in all other degrees; an equivariant coefficient map induces that same map in degrees zero and one. It commutes with $\tau-1$. Its cohomology is $T^0(M)=\ker(\tau-1)$, $T^1(M)=M/(\tau-1)M$, and $T^q(M)=0$ for $q\geq2$. The first is $M^G$: a vector fixed by $\tau$ is fixed by every integer multiple of $\tau$, and its stabilizer is closed as well as open (the complement of an open subgroup is a union of open cosets), hence contains the closure of that dense cyclic subgroup. This identification is natural in coefficient maps.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph; explicit construction of the two-term functor

proof.text: A short exact sequence in $\mathcal C$ is short exact on underlying $A$-modules by [lem-exc-discrete-modules-abelian], so applying $K$ gives a degreewise short exact sequence of complexes (the original sequence in degrees zero and one and the zero sequence elsewhere). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] to obtain its connecting maps, and [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-long-exact-naturality] to obtain their naturality. There is an initial zero because these complexes have no negative terms: the map on their degree-zero kernels is the restriction of the original injection and is injective. The maps on $T^0$ and $T^1$ are induced by the coefficient maps on a kernel and a quotient, so they preserve addition of maps; the higher functors are zero. Thus these functors and connecting maps satisfy precisely [def-weil-pbc-delta-functor].

Apply [lem-exc-coinduced-discrete-embedding] to obtain the discrete continuous $A[G]$-module $D(M)=\operatorname{Cont}(G,M)$ with action $(g\cdot f)(x)=f(x+g)$ and the equivariant $A$-linear injection $\iota_M(m)(x)=x\cdot m$. For any $f\in D(M)$, [lem-exc-coinduced-functions-open-stabilizer] gives an open subgroup $U$ with $f(x+u)=f(x)$ for $u\in U$. By the neighbourhood basis in Step 1 choose $r\geq1$ with $\ell^rG\subseteq U$. Consequently $f$ factors through reduction $G\to\mathbf Z/\ell^r\mathbf Z$: two lifts of the same residue differ by an element of $\ell^rG$.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph; open-stabilizer factorization supplied by the existing generic nodes

proof.text: Write $L=\ell^r$ for the modulus obtained in Step 3 and $N=\ell^{r+s}=L\ell^s$. Pull $f$ back to $\mathbf Z/N\mathbf Z$. Each residue modulo $L$ occurs $\ell^s$ times, so $\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}f(a)=\ell^s\sum_{a=0}^{L-1}f(a)=0$, since $\ell^sM=0$. On representatives $0\leq a<N$ set $h(a)=\sum_{b=0}^{a-1}f(b)$, with empty sum zero. For $a<N-1$ subtraction gives $h(a+1)-h(a)=f(a)$; for $a=N-1$ the zero total sum gives $h(0)-h(N-1)=f(N-1)$. Thus $h$ is well defined on the cyclic quotient, and its pullback is continuous because that quotient is finite discrete. With the translation action it satisfies $(\tau-1)h(x)=h(x+1)-h(x)=f(x)$. Therefore $\tau-1:D(M)\to D(M)$ is surjective.

source.place: Proof, third paragraph, explicit periodic partial-sum construction including the wraparound equation

proof.text: Step 4 gives $T^1(D(M))=0$, and $T^q(D(M))=0$ for $q\geq2$ already follows from the definition of $K$. The injection $\iota_M$ of Step 3 therefore induces zero in every positive degree. The category $\mathcal C$ is abelian by Step 1 and $A\text{-Mod}$ is abelian; Step 2 supplies a cohomological delta-functor. All hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-effaceable-delta-functor-universal] now hold, and hence $T$ is universal.

source.place: Tag 010T, lemma-efface-implies-universal; applied to the effacement constructed in the blueprint third paragraph

proof.text: Let $C(M)^n=\operatorname{Cont}(G^n,M)$ with the inhomogeneous differential of [lem-exc-continuous-cochains-delta-functor]. This node supplies its complex functor and its cohomological delta-functor $S^q=H^q(C(-))$. For $q>0$, [lem-exc-coinduced-continuous-acyclic] gives $S^q(D(M))=0$ for exactly the translation action used in Step 3. The natural monomorphism in [lem-exc-coinduced-discrete-embedding] therefore effaces every positive $S^q$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-effaceable-delta-functor-universal] again to conclude that $S$ is universal. In degree zero the given differential is $d^0m(g)=g\cdot m-m$, so its kernel is $M^G$, with no incoming boundaries. Thus $S^0$ and $T^0$ have the same natural identification with invariants.

source.place: Tag 0DVG, section-continuous-group-cohomology, displayed differential and discrete-module delta-functor; coinduced effacement from the cited existing nodes

proof.text: Define a natural map of complexes $e_M:C(M)\to K(M)$ by $e_M^0=\operatorname{id}_M$ under $C(M)^0=M$, $e_M^1(f)=f(\tau)$, and $e_M^n=0$ for $n\geq2$. Its only nontrivial differential equation is $e_M^1(d^0m)=\tau\cdot m-m=d_K^0(e_M^0m)$; in positive degrees both sides of the remaining equations are zero. Evaluation is $A$-linear and commutes with postcomposition by every coefficient map, so this is a natural chain map. The induced map in degree-zero cohomology is the identity on $M^G$.

source.place: Proof, final identification clause; explicit comparison chain map supplied by the agent

proof.text: For every short exact coefficient sequence, [lem-exc-continuous-cochains-short-exact] gives the degreewise short exact sequence of $C$-complexes, and Step 2 gives that of $K$-complexes. Naturality of $e$ makes its three components a morphism between these two sequences. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-long-exact-naturality] to obtain $H^{q+1}(e_{M'})\circ\delta_S^q=\delta_T^q\circ H^q(e_{M''})$. Hence $H^\bullet(e):S\to T$ is a morphism of delta-functors with degree-zero component the identity.

source.place: Tag 0117, lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain, functoriality applied to the explicit comparison map

proof.text: By universality of $T$ there is a morphism $u:T\to S$ extending the inverse degree-zero identification. The two composites $u\circ H^\bullet(e)$ and $H^\bullet(e)\circ u$ extend the identities in degree zero. By uniqueness for the universal delta-functors $S$ and $T$, respectively, each composite is the identity. This uses exactly the universal property in [def-weil-pbc-delta-functor], furnished in Steps 5 and 6 by [lem-weil-pbc-effaceable-delta-functor-universal]. Thus every $H^q(e_M)$ is an isomorphism, so $e_M$ is a quasi-isomorphism and becomes an isomorphism in the ordinary derived category by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The continuous-cochain description of [def-exc-continuous-cohomology] identifies $C(M)$ as the complex computing the continuous cohomology in the statement. Consequently $K(M)=[M\xrightarrow{\tau-1}M]$ computes it as well, naturally in $M$; in particular $H^0(G,M)=\ker(\tau-1)$, $H^1(G,M)=\operatorname{coker}(\tau-1)$, and $H^q(G,M)=0$ for $q\geq2$.

source.place: Proof, third paragraph, final identification; universal-property argument and comparison quasi-isomorphism made explicit
